meta.title: Wallet Access Recovery | Lenix Protocol
meta.description: Recover access to software and hardware wallets when passwords are lost or files are damaged. Viability assessed first. You keep control of your assets.

Hero.subtitle: Forgotten passwords, corrupted wallet files, and partial backups — not exchange login resets or wallets belonging to someone else. We assess whether recovery is realistic before paid work begins.

Audiences.title: Common situations we review
Audiences.description: Most clients still have a wallet file, device, or backup fragment. They lost the password, PIN path, or readable seed — not the underlying ownership.

password.title: Forgotten wallet password
password.desc: Software wallets such as MetaMask keystores, Electrum, or Bitcoin Core where the file exists but the encryption password is lost.

file.title: Damaged or partial files
file.desc: Corrupted wallet.dat files, incomplete backups, or metadata recovered from an old device that may still hold the key material.

estate.title: Estate and legal matters
estate.desc: Executors, trustees, or counsel who need documented access paths for a deceased or incapacitated holder's wallet — with proper authorization.

treasury.title: Operational wallet lockout
treasury.desc: Teams that lost credentials to a treasury or operations wallet and need a controlled recovery process with audit-friendly handling.

Boundaries.subtitle: Wallet recovery is a common scam category. Lenix only takes cases with clear ownership, documented authorization, and a technical path worth attempting.

ownership.title: Provable ownership required
ownership.desc: We work on wallets you own or are legally authorized to recover — not third-party addresses or credentials obtained without consent.

assessment.title: Viability before fees
assessment.desc: We review wallet type, backup state, and password hints before scoping paid decryption work. Hopeless cases are declined early.

no_custody.title: You move the assets
no_custody.desc: When access is restored, you transfer funds yourself. Lenix does not take custody of recovered cryptocurrency.

no_scam.title: No remote-access tricks
no_scam.desc: We do not ask for screen sharing, verification deposits, or advance unlock fees — patterns used by fraudulent recovery sites.

decline.title: Cases we usually decline
decline.desc: Public address only, wallet files bought online, or hardware wallets with lost PIN and no backup are typically not recoverable.

confidential.title: Controlled handling
confidential.desc: Wallet materials are processed in a defined chain of custody with access controls — not passed through informal channels.

Process.title: From assessment to access
Process.description: A structured path designed for holders and authorized representatives — not open-ended brute-force promises.

submit.title: Submit case details
submit.desc: Wallet type, what backup material exists, and any password hints or patterns you remember. Initial viability review is part of intake.

scope.title: Scope and feasibility
scope.desc: We tell you plainly if decryption is worth attempting, expected effort, and fees — before you commit to paid work.

recover.title: Controlled recovery
recover.desc: If engaged, decryption runs in a controlled environment. You regain access and move assets on your own schedule.

Support.title: Wallet types we commonly see
Support.description: Coverage depends on file format, backup completeness, and encryption strength. Confirm yours during intake.

software.title: Software wallets
software.desc: Bitcoin Core, Electrum, MetaMask JSON keystores, Exodus backups, and similar locally encrypted wallet files.

hardware.title: Hardware devices
hardware.desc: Select cases involving damaged Ledger or Trezor devices where chip data or backups may still yield a recovery path — not lost PIN with zero backup.

formats.title: Legacy and custom
formats.desc: Older wallet.dat variants, BIP38-encrypted keys, and enterprise vault exports — assessed individually.

Cta.title: Have a wallet file but lost access?
Cta.subtitle: Describe the wallet type and what backup material you still have. We will tell you if a recovery path exists before any paid engagement.
